pr_title: Fix 500 Error with branch and tag sharing the same name
pr_body:
Fixed 500 error while create Pull request when there are more
than one sources (branch, tag) with the same name
The idea is to take branch instead of tag by default if the branch and tag name are equal

Fix #15592

Signed-off-by: Viktor Yakovchuk <viktor@yakovchuk.net>

Hmm... Do we ever not want to push to refs/heads? I suspect we should be making this determination before push fails in the first place.

> 
> I'll have a look.

Yes we want to push without "refs/heads" when we create Pull request from tag instead branch. If we always push with refs/heads we will be not able to create pull request from tag.
I would guess that we should be setting the correct ref in the PR instead.

As I understand it, you will have to rewrite a lot, especially the routing system, to understand from tag or branch we do Pull request. And as I see GitHub use similar routes and take branch as default when the branch and tag names are equal.

I think the pr.HeadBranch and pr.BaseBranch should have had the refs/heads/... in them and I am fairly certain that at some point I forcibly added this. Somewhere along the line this appears to have been dropped - which is fairly disappointing as this is precisely why I would have added this.

Hello, it seems to me that we have 2 options for solving the #15592:

- this patch, perhaps with additional changes recommended by you
- adding refs/heads wherever such operations occur

Еhe second option makes it impossible to create a PR from the tag, but I can see from code and interface that this functionality is planned, although it does not work yet.

I am ready to implement both options in a few days, which one should I choose?

@zeripath @lunny guys which way we choose to solve this problem?
1. We delete tags tab from source selector when create pull request (in all over cases we keep all as it is) sea also #15695 Also add "refs/heads" to the code.
2. We take my pull request and fix pull request from tag (now it doesn't work)

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/20933795/120920050-82306a00-c6c5-11eb-9719-01ab23088fa9.png)

I am ready to prepare new PR after we choose a way to solve the problem.

OK you have a working fix that fixes the problem for now so I suspect we should merge this.

However, my suggestion is that we should be putting the correct thing in the PR from the start.

So, if you are creating a PR from a branch - then it gets the full ref name: refs/heads/branch.

If you are creating a PR from a tree - it's the full sha

If it's a tag then it's refs/tags/xxx

And so on.

The PR has to be correct and correct forever.

if we use aliases then as you've shown it breaks everything because the name is not a full unambiguous ref.
@techknowlogick  please take a look once time permit.

issue_context.body:
- Gitea version (or commit ref): 1.14.1
- Git version: 2.30.2
- Operating system: docker image gitea/gitea:1

- Database:
  - [ ] PostgreSQL
  - [ ] MySQL
  - [ ] MSSQL
  - [x] SQLite

- Can you reproduce the bug at https://try.gitea.io:
  - [x] Yes: https://try.gitea.io/berjou/same-tag-and-branch-name-test/pulls
![1619107644](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10575885/115747495-9cbcb700-a395-11eb-8ad1-cb27dee50b54.png)
  - [ ] No
  
- Log gist:
Sorry, tinkering a lot with my setup right now, the log are no longer present on my machine, and since the issue is easily reproductible, it should not be a problem. However, I'm happy to provide you specific logs if needed.

## Description
- `git checkout -b same-tag-and-branch-name-test`
- Create a commit and `git push origin same-tag-and-branch-name-test`
- `git tag same-tag-and-branch-name-test`
- `git push origin tag same-tag-and-branch-name-test`
- Create a pull request to merge `same-tag-and-branch-name-test` into `master`
- Now `https://gitea-instance/user/repo/pulls` return an error 500
- Note that we can see the pull request by accessing `https://gitea-instance/user/repo/1`

Notes:
After deleting the branch and tag, pushing my commit to a new brarnch with a different name, and opening a new pull request, the error 500 on `https://gitea-instance/user/repo/pulls` is gone. However, after merging the merge request, and now that there is no more opened PR, the error 500 came back.

Hope this issue can be fixed, and that someone could help me to fix my broken repository.
